summary: The SELF DRIVE Act of 2026 amends title 49 of the United States Code to regulate vehicles equipped with automated driving systems (ADS). It directs the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to establish new safety standards, safety case requirements, and a National Automated Vehicle Safety Data Repository for reporting covered crashes. It also sets rules for testing, evaluation, and limited commercial operations of automated vehicles while adjusting federal preemption over certain state laws.

affected_groups.effect: Must develop safety cases, comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards, report covered crashes and quarterly mileage data to a national repository, and adhere to federal regulations.
affected_groups.group: Manufacturers of automated driving systems and ADS-equipped vehicles

affected_groups.effect: Must issue final rules regarding safety standards and the safety data repository by specific deadlines, review definitions, and oversee testing, evaluation, and commercial operations.
affected_groups.group: The Secretary of Transportation and the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from banning ADS vehicles with valid safety cases or requiring separate crash reporting, but maintain authority over traditional areas like traffic laws, registration, insurance, and emissions inspections.
Must review the implementation of the connected vehicles final rule within one year and brief relevant congressional committees.

key_provisions: Requires manufacturers of automated driving systems or ADS-equipped vehicles to develop a safety case and provide it to the Secretary of Transportation upon request.

Requires the Secretary of Transportation to issue a final rule establishing a National Automated Vehicle Safety Data Repository by September 30, 2026, to collect crash reports and quarterly mileage data.
Allows the Secretary of Transportation to authorize manufacturers conducting testing or evaluation to undertake limited commercial operations, including carrying passengers or freight.

Preempts state and local laws that prohibit the sale, introduction into commerce, or importation of ADS-equipped vehicles with an approved safety case, or laws that require reporting covered crashes to states.

Preserves state and local authority over traffic laws, vehicle registration, safety and emissions inspections, congestion management, insurance, consumer protection, environmental laws, and dealer/distributor regulations.
Requires the Secretary of Commerce to review the implementation of a specific connected vehicles final rule within one year and brief designated congressional committees.
Provides exceptions regarding making manual control devices inoperative when an automated driving system is safely engaged and performing the driving task.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts, authorization levels, or appropriations required to establish and maintain the National Automated Vehicle Safety Data Repository and federal oversight.
Specific civil penalties or fine amounts for non-compliance with the new reporting or safety case requirements.
